acceptedSurfaceOwners.note: Existing singleton-daemon/PID-lock behavior is closed and cannot be re-owned through configuration-runtime subtraction.
Existing many-client/server foundation behavior is closed even though no local task card is used here to infer an upstream path partition.
Typed layered configuration and feature flags are closed; residual OpenCode config discovery is not automatically an OPS owner.
Runtime lifecycle-manager behavior is closed and must not be reopened through source-family overlap.
The existing EffectRunner adapter is closed; configuration-runtime membership does not authorize a second generic runtime adapter.

reviewedPartitions.behavior: Location-scoped config discovery reads global/project/.opencode documents once, applies specificity ordering and loads policy rules.
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: OPS-001 and OPS-005 have the same live surface signature; accepted BASE configuration/lifecycle owners also overlap this surface, and no task-specific source binding chooses this partition.

reviewedPartitions.behavior: State.create serializes materialization, composes scoped transforms, removes them on scope finalization and supports batched reload coalescing.
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: This reusable runtime primitive is consumed by other domains; no residual OPS task names or owns it.

reviewedPartitions.behavior: A location-keyed service graph is hoisted/compiled with replacements and retained by LayerMap with a 60-minute idle TTL.
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The Session spec defines Location service lifetime, not a residual OPS story. Assigning it to OPS-001/005/004/008 from membership would invent task ownership.

reviewedPartitions.behavior: Global bootstrap derives XDG/process paths and creates runtime directories; npm configuration reads process environment; the reviewed installation slice is only version/channel metadata.
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: This evidence crosses process bootstrap/configuration and only a small part of installation. It cannot distinguish either identical residual OPS group or authorize the unreviewed installation remainder.

reviewedPartitions.behavior: Repository references normalize supported forms, reject unsafe branches and derive branch-isolated cache paths/identities before materialization.
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: This is the strongest small strict-TDD-friendly fragment, but repository-operations maps the same source family to OPS-002/003/004/006/008 and no task/path evidence chooses one.

reviewedPartitions.behavior: RepositoryCache serializes checkout materialization behind a file lock and performs stale removal, clone/fetch/checkout/reset plus Git-derived result projection.
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The contract violates the authorized no-network boundary and remains shared across multiple residual OPS ids plus frozen INT-002/OPS-007/OPS-009 overlap.

candidateFragments.inputs: repository reference string, optional branch and cache root
candidateFragments.outputs: normalized reference, typed validation failure, branch-isolated cache path and stable cache identity
candidateFragments.failureSemantics: invalid references and unsafe branches are rejected deterministically; parser returns absence for unsupported malformed forms
candidateFragments.stateLifetime: none for validation/cache identity; GitHub default remote construction can consult process environment
candidateFragments.resourceLifetime: bounded input strings and path construction only
disqualifiers: OPS-002/003/006 have identical repository-only surface signatures.
OPS-004/008 also include this surface and are mutually indistinguishable.
No task card, worklog, requirement or pinned task/path specification selects this fragment for one OPS id.

candidateFragments.inputs: initial state factory, draft adapter, optional finalizer and scoped transform callbacks
candidateFragments.outputs: materialized current state plus transform registration/disposal and explicit reload
candidateFragments.failureSemantics: transform failures are converted to fatal Effect failure in the upstream primitive; reloads are serialized
candidateFragments.stateLifetime: in-memory state and transform list live with the service; each transform lives with its owning Scope
candidateFragments.resourceLifetime: single in-memory semaphore plus batched reload set
disqualifiers: The primitive is a reusable caller-neutral runtime mechanism rather than a task-specific OPS contract.
OPS-001 and OPS-005 are surface-identical and OPS-004/008 also overlap configuration-runtime.
Accepted BASE runtime/configuration owners remain closed and cannot be reassigned by subtraction.

historyReview.limitation: The pinned local OpenCode checkout exposes the locked commit but is not used to infer missing task ownership from unavailable historical intent.

closureCriteria: An OPS-001/002/003/004/005/006/008 ownership change requires new pinned task-specific source/path evidence, not surface subtraction, equivalence-group membership, requirement arithmetic or task-number inference.
The candidate must have direct task-specific source, caller, test and genuine specification evidence with explicit inputs, outputs, failure semantics, state/resource lifetime and bounded authority.

Accepted BASE owners and frozen INT-002/OPS-007/OPS-009 contracts must remain excluded; no candidate may silently require network, credentials, user-DB mutation, UI/browser state, process mutation or unapproved dependencies.
Every unresolved partition and unresolved rule remainder must receive a source-grounded task disposition or remain explicitly blocked before an operations family can be called exhausted.
